reason: A: the spacing is uneven. There is a big dead gap between the can and the headline and another between the headline and the subcopy, while the subcopy sits jammed against a shrunken CTA. The subcopy and button text are also small for a story format, so the type cluster looks like a scaled-down copy. B: the can, headline and CTA are bigger and better grouped, with consistent vertical rhythm. Its flaws are the headline breaking so that 'fizz' sits alone on the second line and a slightly tight stack between the headline, subcopy and CTA.

Both cram every original element into the leaderboard as five narrow columns. The body copy is as loud as the headline, 'Ships late June' is squeezed into a three-line sliver, the legal text is illegibly tiny, and the small CTA is pinned into the top-right corner with no breathing room. A at least centres the sun logo and SOLSTICE wordmark in the dark brand block. In B the logo drifts off-centre and the wordmark is half-lost at the bottom of the block, while the larger headline jams against the top and bottom edges.

A: the 'Reserve a Case' CTA has shrunk to an unreadable pill, and the body copy is set almost as large as the headline, which flips the hierarchy. The 'Limited Summer Release' eyebrow and 'Ships late June' are illegible specks, and the legal text competes in the right column. B has the same oversized body copy, unreadable eyebrow and legal clutter, but its CTA is a properly sized, readable orange button, so the action at least stands out.

A: the dark header bar doesn't span the canvas (gaps at left and right) and the logo is shrunk to a tiny mark. The headline is undersized, with oversized empty gaps around it, and 'Ships late June' has drifted down next to the legal text instead of sitting under the CTA. B: the header is also misaligned and lopsided (a bigger gap on the right), and 'Ships late June' floats alone in dead space far below the button. Even so, B's headline is larger, which gives a clearer hierarchy, and the headline, body copy and CTA are grouped more tightly.

I scored both 2 out of 5. Both drop the Solstice logo and the dark brand header. Both also shrink the body copy and legal text to an unreadable size in the tiny banner, and in both the legal text is nearly as prominent as the body copy. A keeps the orange 'Limited Summer Release' eyebrow and leaves a clear gap between the headline and the body copy. B appears to lose the eyebrow, and its body copy starts against the headline with no gutter. B's CTA and legal block also look jammed together, so A is the less broken of the two.

A: the red sale banner runs into the can's sun and lid. The whole content column is pushed left, leaving the right half empty apart from the planet, and the logo floats at the top right with no alignment to anything. The legal line sits between the headline and the CTA at near-body size, which pushes the CTA down to the bottom edge and breaks the hierarchy. B: the can, headline and CTA are centred and read in a clear order, and the headline stands out strongly. However, the legal text is jammed right under the headline and is too large, the shrunken sale banner loses its prominence, and the logo is placed off-grid at the top right.

Both use the same weak banner layout. The legal fine print is stacked into a four-line block in the prime left slot and is unreadable at this size. The SOLSTICE logo and the product can are shrunk to specks, and the headline is the only thing that reads. In A, the 'LONGEST DAY SALE' ribbon is a tiny, illegible sliver jammed under 'longer', close to colliding with it. In B, the ribbon is slightly larger and its text is legible. It is still small, though, and its tilt crowds the bottom edge. That makes B marginally less bad.

Both share the same breaks: the body copy sits on top of the teal circle at the far left, the circle is split off from the can it should frame, the body copy comes before the headline in reading order, the GLACIER wordmark sits below the headline, and the CTA and chips are crammed together edge to edge. A spreads these pieces across the width with large dead gaps around a tiny floating can. B groups the can, headline and buttons more tightly but leaves an empty band at the right, so it is only marginally better.

A: the headline is blown up almost to the full width, with tiny side margins, and it is jammed against the top edge. The subcopy and CTA row sits right-aligned and crammed under it, which breaks the centred axis and leaves no breathing room at the bottom. B: the headline is centred at a sensible size with good margins and clear hierarchy, but there is a large dead gap between the headline and the bottom row, and the subcopy and CTA group sits slightly left of centre.

A keeps a strong two-line headline that clearly dominates the CTA, but the whole stack is crammed: the headline nearly touches the top edge, there's only a small gap above the CTA, and the button sits about 10px from the bottom edge. B's single-line headline suits the banner width better, but it's now small next to an oversized CTA, so the hierarchy is weaker. B's spacing is also lopsided, with a large top margin and a big gap above the CTA while the button is jammed against the bottom edge. Both are centred stacks, not a real left-to-right banner layout.

A holds a clean shared left edge (logo, headline, subhead and pills all at x≈131) and its spacing is even. Its flaws are the CTA, which floats on the right between the subhead and the flavour pills and breaks the reading order, and the lower-right area, which feels empty. B's headline is oversized and runs to within about 30px of the right edge. Its left edges don't match (the headline starts at x≈64, everything else at x≈76), and its bulky CTA crowds the subhead, so the layout looks cramped and unaligned.

A is evenly spaced, with a clear stack from logo to headline to subhead to CTA to pills, but its CTA floats awkwardly at the right above the pills: its left edge matches Honey Rosemary but its right edge doesn't. That leaves a large empty space at the top right, and the peach circle is cropped to a small stub in the corner. B makes the headline and CTA bigger, but the headline runs nearly to the right edge, so the margins are uneven. Its oversized CTA is also squeezed between the subhead and the pills with very little gap and doesn't line up with the pill row, so it feels cramped and less deliberate than A.

A has a strong three-line headline, but the subhead (x≈70) is out of line with the headline (x≈88). The flavour pills are staggered at random (Blood Orange alone on one row, Cucumber Mint indented at x≈106), the CTA floats on the right with nothing to align to, and about 80px at the bottom is dead space. B has the same ragged pill rows and subhead misalignment, plus an awkward headline break ('Summer / flavours are here'). B also has uneven vertical gaps: a large hole under the headline and loose spacing around the CTA and pills. Its smaller CTA weakens the hierarchy, so it looks more scattered than A.

Both candidates are visually identical. Both have the same flaws: the can sits in the upper part of the brown circle, leaving its lower half as empty dead space. The SOLSTICE logo is placed beside the attribution 'THE SOLSTICE TASTING TEAM' and competes with it, instead of sitting apart as a brand sign-off. There is also a large, unbalanced gap between the quote mark and the quote text, and the quote block is not vertically centred against the circle.

A: the quote is large, reads well and has a clear hierarchy. However, the attribution is indented about 20px from the quote's left edge, so the two don't align, and it sits right against the top of the circle. The can and logo look a little arbitrarily placed inside the big circle. B: the attribution is cut off from its quote and floats centred above the circle, separated from the quote by a large dead gap, which breaks the grouping. The logo strip is stuck in the middle of the circle, off any grid, and the can and its SOLSTICE label are shrunk.

The two layouts are nearly the same, and both have the same main faults. The logo is jammed against the canvas edge and touches the headline. The SAVE badge floats over the body copy and crowds it. The coffee bag is a tiny sliver cut off at the right edge, so the product is lost. A's CTA button is undersized and weak. B's larger CTA gives slightly better hierarchy, but its oversized badge competes with the headline and nearly touches the copy below it.

A: the headline is undersized for a square and the NEW VIDEO badge floats out of line with the logo row. The big lime circle crowds the bottom-left, and 'Full review inside.' hangs alone to its right in dead space, so the layout feels lopsided. B: the headline is bold and fills the width, giving clear hierarchy, and the badge lines up with the logo. However, the circle and product have shrunk until they feel minor, and 'Full review inside.' still floats unanchored beside the circle, leaving empty areas on the right and at the bottom.

A: the phone mockup is jammed against the top and bottom edges, the headline is undersized for the banner, and the '7 days free' fine print is too small to read; the dead gap between the phone and the text also weakens it. Still, the headline, subtext and CTA sit in a balanced left-to-right flow. B has the same cramped phone and tiny fine print, and it is worse on grouping: the subtext floats far below the headline, and a huge empty gap between the headline and the CTA leaves the button isolated and the layout lopsided.

Both use the same left-to-right banner layout: headline, a tiny phone, the CTA, then fine print. In both, the phone is too small to read and is reduced to a smudge, and the '7 days free, then 6/month' fine print wraps awkwardly onto three lines and is pushed against the right edge. B places the phone almost against the CTA button, which makes the middle feel crowded, and changes the button text's capitalisation ('Try it Free'). A spaces the headline, phone and button slightly more evenly.

A fills the tall canvas well. The can is large and keeps its proportions, and the type is a good size. Its flaws: the headline breaks with 'fizz' alone on the second line, and the subcopy and CTA are cramped together near the bottom while the space under the can is generous. In B the headline is cut off from its subcopy by a large gap, so the text group falls apart. B's can, subcopy and CTA are also undersized, which leaves dead space and weakens the hierarchy compared with the original.

Both use the same cramped five-column leaderboard. 'Ships late June' wraps into a stacked three-word orphan, the legal block is unreadably tiny and gets as much space as the CTA, and the small 'Reserve a Case' button is pushed into the far corner. In A, the headline nearly touches the top and bottom edges, and the sun mark sits awkwardly in the dark logo panel. B gives the headline a little more breathing room and centres the logo better, but its body copy is almost as heavy as the headline and runs close to the top edge, so the two compete for attention.

A: the headline fills the canvas, but the 'Limited Summer Release' eyebrow and the divider are shrunk to an unreadable orange speck. Both have the same broken header: the dark band doesn't reach the canvas edges and leaves cream gaps at the sides, and the logo is shrunk. B shrinks the headline so it barely outweighs the wide-set body copy, scatters the blocks with uneven gaps, and pushes 'Ships late June' down onto the legal text, away from its button. A wins narrowly because its hierarchy holds up better.

A: the three-line serif headline fills the left edge and touches the top. The body copy and legal text are squeezed to microscopic, unreadable sizes. The 'Reserve a Case' CTA is a tiny pill lost beside the fine print, and the SOLSTICE logo is reduced to an unreadable dark sliver, so the brand and hierarchy are broken. Its saving graces are a visible orange 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' eyebrow and a larger, readable CTA pill, so it is the less bad of the two, though it is still not shippable.

A keeps a centred stack with a strong headline and CTA, but the legal line is oversized, sits between the headline and the CTA and is jammed right under the headline, and the small sale banner top-left reads as detached from the logo top-right. Both banners have the same structural problems. The legal fine print sits at the far left at roughly body-text size, so it competes with the headline. Both break the layout the same way. The body copy sits on top of the teal circle, cut off from the can it belongs with. GLACIER drops below the headline, so the reading order is reversed. A keeps a centred headline with good margins, but the gap between the headline and the subcopy+CTA row is too large, and that row sits slightly left of the headline's centre axis. Its subcopy and CTA are jammed right under the headline and pushed against the right edge, so the layout feels cramped and overstuffed.

A: the one-line headline suits the banner shape, but it shrinks to roughly the button's height, so the CTA pill competes with it for attention. The gap between headline and button is tight, and the top and bottom margins are thin (about 20px and 10px), so the composition feels jammed rather than intentional.

A: the oversized headline almost touches the right edge, and its left edge (~65px) doesn't line up with the logo and subhead (~76px). A: the subhead (x≈60) and the pills (65 vs 88) don't line up with the headline/logo edge (88), there is a large dead gap between the headline and the subhead, the pills are scattered in a ragged staircase, and there is empty space at the bottom. A: the headline is strong and the margins are clean, but the product circle has shrunk into a minor bottom-left element. A: the headline is undersized for the banner height, and the tiny fine print floats about 30px below it, so the two don't read as one group. A: the product is large and fills the narrow canvas well, but the headline breaks into 'Garden-fresh / fizz', leaving 'fizz' alone on its own line. A: the headline is oversized and fills almost the full height, so it nearly touches the bottom edge and the body column ('Small-Batch' almost meets 'released in'). A keeps the logo legible and wraps the headline cleanly into 3 lines, but the spacing is uneven: there is a large dead gap between the phone and the headline, the subhead is nearly as big as the CTA, and the legal text is jammed under the button and against the bottom edge. A: the banner reads left to right with clean margins, but the headline is undersized for the format. Both 320x50 versions have the same broken hierarchy. A: the text column is indented about 108px from the left edge, but the SOLSTICE logo sits at about 50px and is left on its own in the bottom-left corner, so they don't share an edge. A: the quote is set small and the attribution floats far below it, with a big gap that breaks the grouping. A: The quote keeps its quote mark and stays grouped with its attribution, but it is tiny at 320x50, and the attribution sits at the left edge, out of line with the indented quote. A: the headline is huge and leaves almost no gap before the right column; the period of 'sunshine.' nearly touches the CTA.
